instruction: Represent a playing card as a number by packing its suit into two low bits and its rank into the next four bits. Implement functions to create a card and recover its suit and rank. Existing Suite and Rank enums are available.
Create a standard 52-card deck by taking the Cartesian product of four suits and ranks Ace through King. Use the existing createCard function for each suit/rank pair.
Implement a pile rule that returns true when the top card is rank 10 or when the top four cards all share the top card's rank. Empty piles must not be burnable.

Implement card dealing for one or more players. Each player receives six hand cards and three face-down cards from the end of a copied deck, and the functions return the remaining deck without mutating the input.

Implement an in-place generic Fisher-Yates shuffle that visits the array from the final element to the second and swaps each item with a uniformly chosen earlier-or-current index. Return the same array.

Update campaign progress after a match. A win advances one tier up to the campaign length and permanently records completion; a hardcore loss resets the tier while preserving prior completion; other losses leave progress unchanged. Also provide a restart operation that resets only the tier.

Persist campaign progress in localStorage under a difficulty-specific key. Loading must tolerate missing, malformed, or unavailable storage, clamp the tier to the valid campaign range, normalize completion to boolean, and otherwise return fresh progress. Saving must not crash if storage fails.

Implement a deterministic seeded RNG abstraction with an inclusive integer method, an in-place Fisher-Yates shuffle, and sampling without replacement by shuffling a copy. Use a 32-bit state so equal seeds reproduce the same sequence.

Define classic, flip, and mixed side-card pools by card family, map each difficulty to a pool, and build a fixed-size deck by repeatedly selecting random cards from that pool through an injected RNG. Expose a helper that creates the player deck for a difficulty.

Choose a Pazaak bot action using its current total, the opponent's standing state, and the best legal hand play. Recover from a bust when possible, play an exact winning total, stand at 20 or when safely ahead, use a stand threshold of 18, and otherwise end the turn.

Add board query helpers that calculate the scaled board center, return active units and empty cells, convert a world position to cell coordinates, and safely retrieve a cell by x/y with bounds checks and row-major indexing.

Track whether a tactics unit has moved or attacked during its turn. Implement reset, move/attack availability checks, a list of currently available actions, a combined has-actions check, and pass behavior that consumes both actions.
Advance a turn manager to the next player using circular indexing, update currentPlayer, and increment the round counter whenever control wraps back to the first player.

Find visible isometric grid cells for a rectangular viewport. Project each map cell to its isometric center, include an offscreen tile cache margin, store visible cells by x:y key, and return both the visible-cell dictionary and min/max grid bounds.

Compute the minimum Euclidean distance between two rectangular game entities by constructing their four grid-space corners and testing every corner pair. Support units, buildings, and vehicles that expose grid position and grid size.

Implement grid direction angle helpers: calculate an optional rotation-compensated angle between two points, calculate direction after isometric projection with a 45-degree adjustment, and convert between radians and degrees while expressing negative radians as positive degrees.

Implement an iterable collection for game objects that flattens additions, delegates forEach/map/reduce, updates every object each frame, removes dead objects, and schedules each removed object's destroy method after 300 ms.

Implement a tracking projectile subclass that can be cloned, assigned a target fluently, and updated to steer toward a live target. Normalize the target vector, compute the desired angle, choose the shortest rotation direction when error exceeds 10 degrees, set angular and linear velocity while turning, and stop angular rotation when aligned.
